evidence.field: shape, Shuowen analysis, and attested senses
evidence.text: The 場 entry shows a small-seal form but no oracle-bone or bronze examples in its listed graphic sequence. It reproduces 說文: “祭神道也。一曰：田不耕。一曰：治穀田也。从土，昜聲。” Its account calls the original sense a level place for ancient sacrifice, cites 孟子 and 漢書, and separately cites 詩經 七月 for the threshing floor. Later examples include a general place, a deer’s resting place, figurative domain, loose soil, and classifier use. These textual loci establish lexicographic attestations, but the page does not date the individual occurrences or prove a complete semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 場

evidence.field: graphic origin and roles of 昜
evidence.text: The entry interprets oracle-bone and early bronze forms of 昜 as 日 plus 丂, which it reads as a tree branch, and says later bronze forms add 彡 for rays. It proposes sunshine as the graphic sense and treats 昜 as an early form underlying 陽 and 暘. These are the database’s analyses of 昜; they do not establish 場 in oracle-bone or bronze writing, nor are they independently decisive about what 昜 originally depicted.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 昜

evidence.field: pronunciations and phonetic role of 昜
evidence.text: For 場 the page gives modern Mandarin cháng/chǎng, Middle Chinese 直良切, 澄母, 陽韻, level tone, open division III. For 昜 it gives modern Mandarin yáng and Middle Chinese 與章切, 以母, 陽韻, level tone. The shared rhyme and syllable shape are consistent with 昜 serving as a phonetic component, although the Middle Chinese initials differ. These categories are from a rhyme-dictionary tradition, not direct recordings of ancient speech.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 場 and 昜 entries

evidence.field: image description, historical scope, and reuse license
evidence.text: The file presents tracings of small-seal-script samples sourced from several named artifacts, including a Qin imperial edict plaque dated about 221 BCE, Qin Duke Jing’s stone chimes dated about 573 BCE, Qin seals and clay seal impressions, and an 1804 calligraphic work. It is a modern vector tracing, not an artifact photograph, and the file page states CC0 1.0. The description does not establish that 場 appears in the file, so it is unsuitable as a character-specific glyph candidate.

evidence.field: modern comparison image and reuse license
evidence.text: This file depicts modern stroke order for 場 in a standard type style and cites contemporary stroke-order references, including Taiwan’s Ministry of Education. It is not a historical glyph or artifact image. The page offers CC BY 3.0 and GFDL licensing; it could illustrate a present-day form but does not explain historical development.

gaps: No historical glyph candidate is proposed: searches found no usable, character-specific image whose identity, source provenance, period, and reuse rights could all be verified. The Commons examples inspected were either unrelated or modern stroke-order art. The harness should not treat a general seal-script sample as an image of 場.
The CUHK entry lists a small-seal example for 場 but its linked image could not be fetched (cache miss); the exact glyph pixels and their source provenance were therefore not inspected here.
No inspected source in this invocation establishes an oracle-bone or bronze form of 場. The cited CUHK page shows neither in its graphic list; the early forms discussed belong to 昜.

The cited early textual uses are named by work and passage, but their precise manuscript or inscription dates are not given on the inspected page. A first surviving attestation date for 場 remains undetermined.

The transition from ritual ground to grain-drying floor, general venue, figurative domain, and classifier has lexicographic examples but not a fully evidenced chronological chain. The cited page does not date individual passages or establish every semantic bridge.

The specific graphic history from 場 to simplified 场, including a derivation from cursive writing, remains unverified by an inspected primary source. The Ministry dictionary page content was not exposed in this web inspection.

No evidence here supports borrowing of the entire 場 graph for another word. 昜 is analyzed as a sound component in a 土-plus-昜 compound; uncertainty about 昜’s earliest referent does not itself undermine that later phonetic role.

limitations.text: No candidate met the requested character identity, source provenance, period, and reuse-rights checks. The CUHK page links a small-seal image for 場, but its image fetch failed, so this is a sourcing limitation rather than proof that no suitable image exists.
The inspected Commons 場 image is a modern stroke-order illustration, not an ancient artifact photograph or a historical form. It may support a modern-form comparison only.
